ai.description: *Megophrys ancrae* is a small toadfrog (snout-vent length ~35 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark, triangular markings. It features a distinctive rostral appendage and prominent, elongated eyelid horns.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys ancrae* is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated, horn-like dermal projections above the eyes, which are significantly longer than those of other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys ancrae* inhabits the primary subtropical evergreen forests of the Namdapha National Park in Northeast India, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Namdapha horned toadfrog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush small invertebrate prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys ancrae* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch size data remains undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys ancrae* is endemic to the Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh, India, occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Megophrys ancrae* is a low-pitched, metallic "tink" sound repeated at irregular intervals, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in dense forest habitats.
